transcript.text: Bosch built-in microwave BFL524MS0B randomly stops part way through cooking, time still on the display. Opening and closing the door lets it carry on. Maybe once every few days.

The door-related behaviour makes an intermittent door-latch/interlock switch fault the leading suspect. Opening and reclosing the door can re-establish a marginal switch contact; the display time remaining fits that better than a complete power loss. Do not remove the casing or try to adjust/test the internal switches—microwaves can retain dangerous high voltage even unplugged. Until it is assessed, I would avoid relying on it unattended, and stop using it if it runs with the door not firmly shut, behaves inconsistently when the door is moved, or shows any burning smell/sparking. 1. When it stops, note whether the light, fan and turntable stop as well, or whether they continue but there is no heat. This separates a door/interlock interruption from a heating-circuit issue.
2. With it switched off and unplugged, inspect only the door edge and the two latch hooks: remove any food debris and check the door shuts squarely with a positive click, without needing lifting or pressure. A loose or inconsistent latch supports the interlock/latch diagnosis. If the door feels sound but the light/fan/turntable continue while heating stops, it needs an engineer to diagnose the high-voltage/control side instead. If those functions stop and restarting the door reliably brings it back, an engineer should inspect the door latch and interlock switch assembly; this is not a safe DIY internal repair.
[Safety panel] Don't remove the microwave's casing or try to repair it inside. Parts inside a microwave can hold a dangerous electric charge even after it's unplugged — have it checked by a qualified engineer.

When it stops the fan and light stop too, as if I'd opened the door, and the start indicator goes off. I cleaned some grease from around the door hooks/latch slots but it's still happened once since. No smell, sparks or tripping.

That suggests the door-interlock path rather than a heating fault: when it stops, the fan and light stop and the start indication goes out exactly as though the door has been opened, while the remaining time stays stored. It needs a microwave engineer to inspect the door latch and interlock switch assembly and confirm which part is intermittently opening. Do not remove the casing or attempt to test or adjust those switches yourself; microwave internal components can retain dangerous high voltage even unplugged. Until repaired, avoid unattended use. Stop using it altogether if it starts behaving as though the door is open when it is firmly shut, if moving the door affects operation, or if there is any burning smell, sparking or damage around the door.

candidates: Intermittent door-latch/interlock switch or latch alignment fault (high)
